title: Publish to a public registry
summary: F-35's registry wizard, one pattern for every feed type with a public upstream: DJDL's djdl-crates to PyPI.org on Oct 2 at its last step (the name claimed, the trusted publisher added through a deep link, the CI step verified, and the per-package approval, irreversible and limited to stable and beta, with a typed confirmation), then the same card at its Approve step for npm to npmjs (@djdl/crate-schema) and a container image to GHCR (Diceroll's table-server).
compare: Reached from the PyPI feed's ⋯ menu ('Publish to PyPI.org…'); crumbs Packages › PyPI › djdl-crates; Distribution accent; Packages active in the sidebar with the count of feeds on Oct 2 (2).
No subtitle: the card's title says Trusted publishing and the steps name the CI workflow. Which tracks go is said once, in the Approve step's chips.
The card head is 'Trusted publishing' with its progress ('3 of 4 done' and a bar) and the precondition: only a Public package can go; djdl-crates is Public since Sep 12.

Steps: Claim the name (a pending publisher reserves djdl-crates for example-org/djdl), Add the trusted publisher on PyPI.org (the exact owner, repository, workflow and environment values, who added it and when, 'Open on PyPI.org'), Verify (what was checked, with the release.yml job: environment pypi, id-token: write, 'pkey feeds publish-public --deliverable pypi.crates').

Approve: chips for what goes (stable; beta as pre-releases) and what never goes (dev, dashed), a warning that it can't be undone (PyPI.org keeps every version; cleanup never deletes them; stopping only stops new versions), a typed confirmation with the package name in a field capped at 400px, and Cancel with 'Approve publishing to PyPI.org' in the card's foot.
After approval, Packages shows 'Also on PyPI.org' on the djdl-crates row and the approval in the feed's foot, and the portal row says 'also on PyPI.org'.

Other public registries (the owner, 2026-10-09: 'We should have an NPM version of this, alongside any other package feeds we support that have upstream options (Docker, for instance)'): a board under the page, one frame per feed type in the PyPI card's pattern at its Approve step. npm to npmjs: @djdl/crate-schema, the @djdl scope owned by the djdl organization, npmjs trusting release.yml in example-org/djdl with provenance, chips 'stable, as latest' and 'beta, as next' and 'dev never goes', 'npmjs never takes the same version number twice.' Container to GHCR: ghcr.io/example-org/table-server, pushed by example-org/diceroll with its own GITHUB_TOKEN (packages: write; no stored secret), chips 'stable, as latest' and 'beta, as beta', 'A public image on GHCR can't be made private again.' Maven Central and crates.io (F-35's next registries) take the same card when a product has those feeds. Docker Hub is not offered: it has no trusted publishing, so it would need a stored registry secret, which F-35 rules out.
Phone: the steps stack, the code scrolls inside its block, and the foot's two buttons take full rows with the primary on top. Wide: the flow keeps the 960px narrow page, so no line stretches.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink and selection is ink, the accent marks context only; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.
Ship builds is one identity (B5): Release cyan rule, chip, tile and nav marker, the Package glyph, crumb '<Product> › Ship builds'; no per-page green or tangerine.

designReview.reviewer: 4 UX designers, triaged by a lead designer
designReview.verdict: Spacing and copy trimmed per the multi-review triage; see findings.

findings.issue: About 700px of canvas empty at wide; Approve is not under the field it confirms; input 8px from the footer on phone.
findings.resolution: Page is .page.form.centered (760, centred in the container); Cancel and Approve sit directly under the field, left-aligned with it (.actions-under), 16px below it on phone with Cancel as a lower-emphasis button.

findings.issue: Subtitle and card header duplicate; the five parameters read as one dense sentence.
findings.resolution: Second subtitle sentence and the card sub-line dropped; warning 'PyPI.org keeps every version it receives. Stopping later only stops new ones.' at 70ch; step 2 is a key/value grid (.kv-grid) with the timestamp right-aligned.

findings.issue: Change the Approve button colour to the amber warning; set the focus ring to the area colour.
findings.resolution: declined: primary actions stay in the service accent; the focus ring is a single kit token.

findings.issue: Hide PyPI parameters behind a 'Details' disclosure (UX1).
findings.resolution: declined: disclosures hide real data; the key/value grid solves the density.

findings.issue: [Wide] Single-column screens hug the left of a 1920 canvas; the rail leaves 600-750px empty.
findings.resolution: Kit: .page.contained (1280, centred), .page.form.centered, and .sticky-rail (360px rail, sticky at top 88px from 1600px); card pairs use .top (align-items:start).
